ing: bone-in or boneless, cut in large chunks
st: Season the lamb with [[2 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] pepper.
Layer half the potatoes in a heavy pot, then the lamb, onions, carrots and thyme.
Top with the remaining potatoes and pour in [[4 cup]] water.
Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then cover and simmer on low for 2 hours.
Test the lamb; it should be tender and reach well over 145°F (63°C). Cook longer if not.
The top potatoes will fall apart slightly and thicken the broth.
Remove the thyme, stir in [[2 tbsp]] parsley and serve in deep bowls.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and dust a baking sheet with flour.
Whisk [[4 cup]] flour, [[1 tsp]] baking soda and [[1 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Make a well and pour in [[1.75 cup]] buttermilk.
Stir with your hand or a fork just until a shaggy dough forms. Do not overmix.
Turn out and shape into a round about 2 inches tall, handling as little as possible.
Cut a deep cross in the top with a floured knife.
Bake 15 minutes, then lower to 400°F (200°C) and bake 25 minutes more.
The loaf should sound hollow when tapped underneath. Cool 20 minutes and serve with butter.
Put potatoes in a pot with cold water and [[1 tsp]] salt. Boil 20 minutes until tender, then drain.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a skillet and cook the cabbage for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the scallions and cook 1 minute.
Mash the potatoes with [[0.75 cup]] warm milk and [[2 tbsp]] butter until smooth.
Fold in the cabbage mixture, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Spoon into a bowl, make a well in the middle and add [[2 tbsp]] butter.
Serve hot, dipping each bite into the melted butter.
Squeeze the grated potato in a clean towel to remove the liquid.
Mix with [[1 cup]] mashed potatoes, [[1 cup]] flour, [[0.5 tsp]] baking soda, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.25 tsp]] pepper.
Stir in 1 egg and [[0.5 cup]] buttermilk to make a thick batter.
Melt [[1 tbsp]] butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Spoon in batter in rounds about 4 inches wide, flattening slightly.
Cook 5 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked through.
Repeat with the remaining [[2 tbsp]] butter and batter, and serve hot.
Brown the sausages and bacon in a Dutch oven over medium heat for 8 minutes. Pour off excess fat.
Layer the onions, potatoes, sausages and bacon in the pot.
Add the thyme, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Pour in [[3 cup]] water so it nearly covers.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 1 hour.
Check the sausages are cooked to 160°F (71°C) and the potatoes are tender.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] parsley and serve in bowls with the broth.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a large skillet and cook the sausages over medium heat for 12 minutes, turning, until browned and 160°F (71°C) inside.
Move to a warm plate. Fry the bacon 4 minutes per side.
In the same pan, fry the black pudding 2 minutes per side.
Add the mushrooms and tomatoes cut side down and cook 4 minutes.
Warm the beans in a small pot.
In a clean pan melt [[1 tbsp]] butter and fry the 4 eggs 3 minutes to your liking.
Toast the bread and spread with [[1 tbsp]] butter.
Season with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.25 tsp]] pepper and plate everything together.
Boil potatoes in salted water with [[1 tsp]] salt for 20 minutes until tender, then drain.
Warm [[0.75 cup]] milk with the scallions in a small pot for 5 minutes.
Let the potatoes steam dry for 2 minutes.
Mash them well, then stir in the hot milk and scallions.
Beat in [[2 tbsp]] butter, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Spoon onto plates, make a well and add [[1 tbsp]] butter to each of 4 portions.
Serve right away while the champ is hot.

ing: such as cod, cut in chunks
st: Steam the mussels in a covered pot with a splash of water for 5 minutes until open. Discard any that stay shut. Remove the meat and strain the liquid.
Melt [[3 tbsp]] butter in a large pot and cook the leek and onion for 6 minutes.
Stir in [[3 tbsp]] flour for 1 minute.
Slowly pour in [[3 cup]] stock and the mussel liquid, stirring until smooth.
Add the potatoes and simmer 12 minutes until tender.
Add the white fish and salmon and simmer gently 5 minutes.
Stir in [[1 cup]] cream, mussels, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and heat through for 2 minutes.
Top with [[2 tbsp]] dill and serve with soda bread.
Soak [[2.5 cup]] dried fruit and [[0.75 cup]] sugar in [[1.5 cup]] hot tea overnight, or at least 4 hours.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Grease and line a 9 by 5 inch loaf pan with [[1 tbsp]] butter.
Stir 1 egg into the fruit mixture.
Mix [[2.5 cup]] flour, [[2 tsp]] baking powder, [[2 tsp]] mixed spice and [[0.25 tsp]] salt.
Fold the dry ingredients into the fruit until just combined.
Pour into the pan and level the top.
Bake 1 hour 15 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cover with foil if it browns too fast.
Cool in the pan 15 minutes. Slice and serve buttered.

ing: or omit for a non-alcoholic version
st: Fill a heatproof glass with hot water to warm it, then pour out.
Add [[2 tsp]] brown sugar to the glass.
Pour in [[0.75 cup]] hot coffee and stir to dissolve the sugar.
Add [[1.5 fl oz]] whiskey and stir.
Whip [[2 tbsp]] cream until just thick but still pourable.
Pour the cream gently over the back of a spoon so it floats on top.
Drink through the cream without stirring.
Heat the oven to 375°F. Rub [[12 tbsp]] cold butter into [[3 cups]] flour with your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs.
Stir in [[6 tbsp]] ice water a spoonful at a time until the dough just holds together. Divide in two, wrap and chill for 20 minutes.
Mix the cake crumbs, raisins, currants, [[2 tsp]] mixed spice, [[0.5 cup]] brown sugar and the milk in a bowl until a stiff, moist paste forms.
Roll half the dough to fit a 9 by 13 inch pan and press it in. Prick the base with a fork.
Spread the fruit filling evenly to the edges. Roll the second piece of dough, lay it on top and press the edges together.
Score the top into squares, brush with a little milk and sprinkle [[1 tbsp]] sugar. Bake 35 minutes until deep golden.
Cool completely in the pan, then cut into bars along the score lines.
nt: Best swap: use gluten free flour blend 1:1 and bread crumbs from gluten free bread for a gluten free version.

st: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease and line a 9 inch round cake tin with parchment.
Beat the butter and brown sugar for 3 minutes until light and fluffy, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and cloves together, then fold into the butter mixture with the milk until just combined.
Fold in two thirds of the diced apples. The batter will be thick.
Spoon half of the batter into the tin, scatter over the remaining apples, then top with the rest of the batter and smooth.
Sprinkle the top with the demerara sugar.
Bake for 55 to 60 minutes until deep golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 15 minutes before turning out.
Serve warm in thick slices with hot custard or cold cream.
nt: Best swap: use two tart baking pears in place of the apples, or vegan butter 1 to 1.
